_README: Pinned corpus projects with a resolvable repo URL, a pre-fix commit, and the
Every field here was verified, not guessed:
commit          exists in the repo and is the last commit BEFORE the audit date
engagement      the corpus engagement_id; the ground truth is that engagement's
own rows, never the whole project's rows across several audits.
ground_truth    severe (critical/high/medium) finding COUNT per class, derived by
running eval/harness.py's PLAYBOOK_MAP over the corpus rows.
It is a set of counts, not an instance list, because the corpus
does not pin each finding to a line of a pinned commit.
eval-class-scoring.md explains why instance-level tp/fp/fn is not claimed.

projects.ground_truth_note: 8 arithmetic + 2 logic_accounting(h) + 2 input_validation, all severe. The remaining logic_accounting rows on this engagement are medium and land on sol.inflation only if their leaf matches PLAYBOOK_MAP.
The commit is the one the audit report itself links to (blob/<sha> appears 88 times in this engagement's body_text), i.e. the exact tree that was reviewed.
projects.build: foundry, needs via_ir = true or solc 0.8.20 fails with 'Stack too deep'

projects.ground_truth_note: The commit is the one the audit report links to (12 references). Hardhat project with no committed lockfile/artifacts, so slither and aderyn could not compile it; only tools/detect.py ran. Kept in the set deliberately: a project where two of three tools are UNAVAILABLE is exactly the case the harness must report as unavailable rather than as a clean zero.
